newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-MUSTER SUFFERS ANOTHER SETBACK ON CLAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER SUFFERS ANOTHER SETBACK ON CLAY.

text.p: Top seed Thomas Muster suffered another blow on his favorite clay surface on Thursday when he was ousted from the Generali Open by Czech Slava Dosedel.
The Austrian was beaten 2-6 6-3 6-4 in the third round of the $535,000 event, saying he especially struggled with Dosedel's returns.
Muster, previously known as the clay-court king following a series of wins in 1995 including the French Open title, ended his clay season with a disappointing nine wins in 18 matches.
He recorded his biggest clay success of the year by reaching the quarter-finals in St.Poelten in mid-May. However, he won two hard court tournaments in Dubai and Key Biscayne earlier in the year.
"I have no problems playing on clay. It is still my favorite surface," said Muster. "My problem at the moment is that I can't take my chances."
"I feel physically fit, even now after three sets. I just need more match practice and I have concentration problems," added the world's number five.
Muster will be playing only on hard courts for the remainder of the year, and next competes in Montreal and Cincinatti to prepare for the U.S. Open.
